name: Middle Low German

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Middle Low German (midd1318).

notes: Research. West Germanic (Ingvaeonic/Low Saxon) medieval stage written in the Latin alphabet. Grapheme map covers the basic vowels, doubled long vowels, the digraphs sch [ʃ], ch [x], ng and ck, and the plain consonants with v and w both mapped to [v]. Middle Low German spelling was not standardised across the Hanseatic writing tradition; vowel length and quality were marked inconsistently and are largely left unencoded, so a notable PER floor is expected. Grapheme table checked against Lasch (1914): no discrepancy found.

stress.notes: Middle Low German, like other West Germanic varieties of its period, keeps the inherited Common Germanic fixed root-initial stress (Lasch 1914). `default_position=1` (first syllable) models this; stress-neutral prefixes and loanwords are not separately handled for lack of a documented closed list in the sources consulted.
